problem:
Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface defined by the equations

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y={v}^{2},\,z=uv,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0,
$$

at the point $(1,4,2).$
worked_solution:
In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,uv⟩,\,u\ge 0,\,v\ge 0.
$$

First, notice that since $(1,4,2)$ lies on the surface, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}=1 \\ {v}^{2}=4 \\ uv=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u=1 \\ v=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these tangent vectors when $u=1$ and $v=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨2(1),\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) & =⟨0,\,2(2),\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,4,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,2)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,2) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-8,\,-2,\,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-4,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ (-8)\cdot (x-1)+(-2)\cdot (y-4)+8\cdot (z-2) & =0 \\ -8x-2y+8z & =0 \\ 4x+y-4z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
